$comment: D-CONFIG-STDIO-STREAM-MACROS-INVISIBLE-ON-ELF: ISO C 7.23.1 requires <stdio.h> to define stdin/stdout/stderr as MACROS, and both ELF references do — glibc writes the self-referential `#define stdin stdin` for exactly that reason. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-27 with a control #error that fired on both: gcc 13.3.0 -std=c2x rc=0, clang 18.1.3 -std=c23 rc=0. DSS answered FALSE on ELF ONLY: src/dss-config/shippedLibs/stdio.json declared the three macros with per-format `variants` for `pe` and `macho` alone, so on ELF the names existed solely as `symbols` — usable in code, invisible to #ifdef. ✔MEASURED before the fix through the shipped CLI, same binary and same source: elf rc=1 with three P001E #error hits; pe rc=0; macho rc=0. The fix is a third `elf` variant per macro, NOT a loader change: the variant selector deliberately has no fallback arm (zero matching variants means the macro is not injected, never a wrong replacement), which is the property that keeps a per-format macro honest. Each #ifdef is folded into the EXIT CODE with a DISTINCT weight (stdin 4, stdout 8, stderr 16, +14 = 42) so a regression names WHICH stream lost its macro — 38, 34 or 26 — rather than only that one did; an #error-based witness could not be a green corpus entry at all. The fputs additionally runs the EXPANSION, which differs in kind per format (elf self-referential and therefore hideset-dependent, pe a call to __acrt_iob_func, macho a rename to __stdoutp), so the asserted bytes prove the macro is usable and not merely defined. RED-ON-DISABLE: drop the `elf` variant from any of the three macros and both ELF arms return 38/34/26 while pe and macho stay 42.
